name: Axiom Grey — Corporate Uniform Subversion
creator: Anonymous; first documented in Axiom Workforce Solutions internal compliance reports, 2205; named by outside observers
description: A clandestine fashion movement in which Axiom Workforce Solutions employees — and later workers across multiple corponations — began making imperceptibly small, technically compliant modifications to mandated corporate uniforms as acts of collective coded resistance. Early iterations included reversed seam allowances visible only under specific lighting, non-standard thread colors in interior linings, and micro-embroideries on collar undersides depicting banned symbols or Shelf solidarity iconography. As the movement matured, practitioners developed an entire sub-language of modification: specific fold patterns, augment-port cover colors, and lapel positioning that could be read by those who knew the code while remaining invisible to compliance scanners and supervisors.
medium: physical garments, covert pattern-sharing via encrypted neural drops, oral tradition in workplace breakrooms
cultural_impact: Became one of the most discussed examples of everyday resistance in GLMZ, demonstrating that fashion could function as a distributed political act requiring no visible protest. Academics and underground journalists wrote extensively about Axiom Grey as proof that corponation control of aesthetics was never total.
controversy: Axiom's compliance division launched 'Operation Seamline' in 2209, deploying high-resolution uniform scanners and threatening termination for non-compliant modifications; the crackdown was partially successful but also dramatically expanded public awareness of the movement. Several workers were terminated and subsequently became prominent figures in Shelf labor advocacy. Axiom's PR response — claiming the modifications were 'a sign of employee creative fulfillment within our culture of belonging' — became one of the most mocked corporate statements in GLMZ media history.
story_hooks: A new Axiom compliance officer is tasked with identifying Axiom Grey practitioners in her district — and slowly realizes her own supervisor's uniform has been coded for years.

A pattern-drop containing a new modification code is intercepted by Axiom security; tracing the drop's origin requires the runner to move through multiple tiers without triggering uniform-scan checkpoints.

A veteran Axiom Grey practitioner with thirty years of service is facing mandatory retirement — and wants to leave behind a single garment encoding the full history of her workplace's resistance movement, but has no one she trusts to receive it.
